modern: The idle business of show, plays on the stage, flocks of sheep, herds, exercises with spears, a bone thrown to little dogs, a bit of bread tossed into fishponds, the labours of ants and their burden-carrying, the scurrying about of frightened little mice, puppets pulled by strings—all alike. It is your duty, then, in the midst of such things to show good humour and not a proud air; but to understand that every man is worth just as much as the things he busies himself about.

explained.summary:
Much of human life looks like a show: parades and plays, animals squabbling over scraps, ants hauling loads, mice scurrying, puppets on strings. Marcus isn’t sneering. He tells himself to move through all this with good humour rather than superiority.

The sting is in the last line: a person is worth about as much as the things they spend themselves on. If you chase trivia, that is your measure.
explained.today: Watching people fight over a parking space, or a group chat erupt over nothing, it’s easy to feel above it all. The better response is a smile, and then a quiet look at what you yourself spend your hours and energy on.
